findings.detail: The close-gap (download) path's response is CloseGapResult.to_dict() whose 'resolution' is the raw SourceResolver to_dict() (close_gap.py:481) and never carries policy_export — only the resolve/ensure CLI branches embed it. So _handle_from_resolution on the close-gap resolution falls back to the legacy <wiki_root>/companies containment and skips the envelope policy_hash cross-check there (expected_policy_hash is None). The N-1 bridge comment's claim 'the CURRENT triplet always sends it' is therefore inaccurate for the close-gap response. Impact for the current triplet is benign: the canonical write root is the company_raw root (companies/...), so the legacy containment passes real downloads, and the wiki-side DL-03 runtime-policy binding (close_gap.py:207-215, pre-existing ZR-404 design) still gates the download against the binding's policy_hash — the failure direction is over-restrictive (deny), never under-restrictive (allow). For future multi-canonical-root configs (e.g. ZR-409 future_lake) this would reject legitimate downloads into policy-allowed non-companies roots. Recommendation: embed policy_export in the close-gap response (or pass the known export hash into the close-gap call) as a follow-up, and cover it with a test.
findings.title: close-gap (download) response lacks policy_export — legacy companies containment still applies on that path
